title: Applied ML Eval: Prompt Sets, Benchmarks, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood's applied-ML evaluation practices covering: eval harness use, prompt set design and benchmarking, model onboarding guidance, quality guardrails, quantization profile considerations, and regression triage procedures. It is intended for ML engineers, applied ML reviewers, and SREs responsible for model quality in production.

Goals

- Provide a repeatable, reviewable process that reduces regressions in production LLM outputs.
- Standardize prompt sets and benchmark metadata so results are comparable across models/versions.
- Integrate quantization and performance trade-offs into eval decisions.
- Define a clear, cross-functional regression triage path with SLAs for investigation and remediation.

Scope and ownership

- Primary owners: Applied ML (model-onboarding, evals) — engineering.
- Secondary stakeholders: SRE (latency/throughput), Product (behavioral requirements), Security & Compliance (data constraints).
- Pages in this playbook: prompt-set catalog conventions, benchmark matrix, onboarding checklist, guardrails, quantization notes, triage runbook.

1) Eval harness: standards and usage

Intro
- The eval harness (repo: infra/eval-harness) is the canonical runner for automated tests and periodic benchmarking. All model onboarding and scheduled checks must use the harness to ensure consistent measurement.

Minimum requirements
- Each eval job must specify: prompt_set_id, seed (optional), metric list, dataset split (train/validation), model_version tag, hardware profile.
- Measurements captured: latency p50/p90/p99 (inference step), tokens_generated, cost_estimate_per_1k_tokens, quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/EM/F1/accuracy/LLR as applicable), hallucination_rate estimate, and regression_score vs baseline.

Quick example: running locally

- CLI: evalctl run --prompt-set prompt_sets/ps-customer-support-v1.yaml --model local:llama-70b:quant=4bit --metrics rouge,f1,accuracy --output results/llama-70b-ps-customer-support-v1.json

Required CI gate
1. All PRs that change model-serving code or prompt sets must include eval harness artifacts or a link to the run in the CI job.
2. Changes that degrade the regression_score by >= 3% relative to baseline must open an ADR and follow the regression triage process below.

2) Prompt sets and benchmarks: design and metadata conventions

Purpose
- Prompt sets should capture realistic production inputs, edge cases, and adversarial examples. They serve as both onboarding checks and recurring regression monitors.

Catalog conventions (YAML metadata example)

- Each prompt set file name: ps-<domain>-<intent>-v<major>.yaml
- Required metadata fields: id, title, domain, intents, tags, owner, created_by, created_at, description, expected_output_format, scoring_fn, baseline_model, sensitivity (low/medium/high).

Example metadata (YAML snippet):

---
 id: ps-customer-support-v1
 title: Customer support - triage and response
 domain: customer_support
 intents: ["greeting", "billing_issue", "cancel_subscription", "product_bug"]
 tags: ["onboarding", "regression-monitor"]
 owner: applied-ml-team
 created_by: aisha.patel@redwood.example.com
 created_at: 2026-11-01
 description: >
   Representative customer support queries sampled from production logs (anonymized). Includes noisy OCR text, misspellings and multi-turn context.
 expected_output_format: json{category: string, resolution: string, follow_up: bool}
 scoring_fn: weighted_accuracy (see scoring functions appendix)
 baseline_model: redwood/redwood-001:v2026-08-15
 sensitivity: high
---

Guidelines for prompt set curation
- Minimum size: 300 examples for high-sensitivity domains (finance, healthcare), 100 examples for general consumer domains.
- Include synthetic adversarial variants (e.g., punctuation/noise/misspells) at 10-20% of set.
- Annotate each example with expected labels and a short explanation for the ground-truth.
- Tag examples that are privacy-sensitive. Sensitive items require reviewer approval and must not be stored in public buckets.

Benchmark matrix and cadence
- Benchmark types:
  - Onboarding benchmarks: run once during model onboarding and pre-rollout (full prompt set suite).
  - Daily smoke: small subset (20-50 examples) to detect regressions quickly.
  - Weekly stability: broader run for metrics drift and cost regressions.

- Schedule: daily smoke (nightly), weekly stability (Sun 03:00 UTC), full onboarding (pre-release).

3) Model onboarding guide (minimum gating checklist)

This checklist is required before a model version is eligible for production rollout. Each item must be documented in the onboarding PR and linked to harness outputs.

Onboarding checklist (must all be Completed or Justified):
- Model metadata: architecture, weights provenance, quantization profile, expected seq-len characteristics, tokenizer version.
- Performance: latency p50/p90 (target depends on tier), throughput benchmarks on target hardware, and cost estimate per 1M tokens.
- Quality: pass onboarding benchmarks with no metric degradation >2% vs baseline for primary metrics; high-sensitivity prompt sets allowed max 1% degradation.
- Safety & policy: safety evals run (to detect hate/toxicity), privacy checks for data leakage.
- Observability: instrumentation for per-request scoring, sampling of outputs, and integration with Redwood Console dashboards (metrics + traces).
- Rollout plan: canary %, rollback criteria, fallback model mapping.
- Compliance: confirm KMS key usage for customer data testbeds (if applicable).

If any gating item fails, the model is blocked from rollout and must follow the regression triage flow.

4) Quality guardrails

Guardrails are automated and manual checks that reduce risk of poor or dangerous outputs. They operate at three levels:
- Pre-request (input sanitization, rate limits, token caps)
- Inference-time (safety filters, constrained decoding, function-calling enforcement)
- Post-request (response filters, reranking, confidence thresholds)

Example guardrail configurations (table):

| Guardrail | Config | Owner | Threshold | Action on breach |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| Hallucination score | model-derived likelihood ratio < 0.01 | applied-ml | high sensitivity sets | rerank with retrieval or fallback model |
| Toxicity filter | classifier score > 0.75 | safety-team | all | hold for manual review + redact |
| Exposure of PII | regex/KMS check positive | security | all | redact and flag incident |

Implementation notes
- Confidence thresholds are tuned per domain and stored in the prompt_set metadata (sensitivity).
- For high-sensitivity workloads, enable automatic reroute to a smaller deterministic policy model if confidence < threshold.

5) Quantization profiles and eval considerations

Trade-offs
- Lower-bit quantization (4-bit, 3-bit) reduces memory and cost but can change generation distribution and token-level likelihoods. Tests must evaluate both quality and per-token calibration.

Quantization evaluation checklist
- Compare quality metrics with float baseline on full onboarding suite.
- Run perplexity-calibration tests, and compute distribution-shift for top-k predictions (KL divergence).
- Validate KV-cache correctness across long-context tests (1000+ tokens) — some quantized kernels exhibit cache-staleness bugs.
- Measure memory, throughput, latency impact (p50/p90) on target hardware.

Recommended metadata fields for quant profiles (stored with model entry):
- quant_profile_id, quant_bits, block_size, kernel_impl, expected_memory_saving_pct, known_limitations, tested_context_lengths, validation_run_id.

6) Regression triage playbook (process and SLAs)

When a regression is detected (automated or manual), follow the triage flow below. The regression triage owner (rotating on-call in applied-ml) must be assigned within 1 hour. Investigation should begin within 4 hours, and a remediation plan within 48 hours.

Detection sources
- Daily smoke failures, weekly stability drift, customer bug reports, SLO breaches logged by Redwood Console.

Triage steps (numbered procedure)
1. Acknowledge: add a ticket in JIRA with tag "eval-regression" and link to failing harness output.
2. Initial classification (within 4 hours):
   a. Is it a data drift/regression (input distribution shift)?
   b. Is it model-induced (new weights/quantization)?
   c. Is it infra-induced (kernel change, runtime bug)?
3. Reproduce locally with the exact harness command and model_version referenced in the failure. Capture logs, traces, and model artifacts.
4. Roll-forward/rollback decision: if degradation caused by recent model change and rollback path is safe, follow canary rollback per rollout plan. If infra bug, open an incident with eng-infra and engage SRE.
5. Root cause analysis (RCA): document findings in the JIRA ticket and update the regression_score and baseline if needed.
6. Remediation and validation: implement fix, run full onboarding and weekly suites, and do post-mortem if severity high.

SLA matrix
- Owner assigned: 1 hour
- Initial classification & reproduce: 4 hours
- Remediation plan: 48 hours
- Critical production blackout remediation: 4 hours (incident path)

Postmortem and continuous improvement
- For all regressions that fail a primary metric by >= 3% or cause customer impact, produce a postmortem within 7 days. Postmortem must include timeline, root cause, corrective actions, and follow-up owners.
- Update prompt sets (add failing examples), adjust guardrail thresholds, or update quantization profile metadata as needed.

Appendices

Scoring functions (short list)
- weighted_accuracy: per-example weights defined in prompt set metadata.
- semantic_similarity: embed + cosine threshold with human-calibrated cutoffs.
- rerank_precision@k: precision among top-k outputs for structured answers.

Common CLI snippets

- Run daily smoke: evalctl run --suite smoke --run-id smoke-$(date +%F) --output s3://eval-results/smoke/
- Compare results: evalctl compare --baseline s3://eval-results/baselines/redwood-001:2026-08-15.json --candidate results/llama-70b-ps-customer-support-v1.json

FAQ
- Q: How large should a prompt set be for general-purpose chat?
  A: 100-300 examples depending on sensitivity. Start with 200 for new domains.
- Q: Who approves a high-sensitivity prompt set?
  A: Two reviewers: applied-ml lead + product owner (see reviewers metadata on the prompt set).
